discovery: Development of massively parallel next-generation DNA sequencing (Solexa/Illumina sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible terminator chemistry)
rationale: Sequencing-by-synthesis is a chemistry-driven method: fluorescent reversible terminator nucleotides plus cluster amplification on surfaces. It cut sequencing costs by orders of magnitude and changed biology and medicine. Balasubramanian and Klenerman have already won major precursor awards (Millennium Technology Prize, Breakthrough Prize), sometimes shared with Mayer. Recent Chemistry prizes went to protein design (2024) and MOFs (2025), which leaves room for a chemical-biology or analytical-method prize. This is a long-standing frontrunner that is still unawarded.
